papers.title_in_file: From membership privacy leakage to Quantum Machine Unlearning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Sec. IV evaluation (MIA, shot-count study, unlearning comparison), Conclusion; derivations and appendix not read
papers.what_it_is: Simulation and cloud-device study of membership inference attacks on quantum neural networks and three unlearning methods.

assertions.value: The authors report that their membership inference attack reached high average success rates of 90% in noiseless simulations and 75.5% on cloud quantum devices.
quotes: the MIA achieved high average success rates of 90% in noiseless simulations and 75.5% on cloud quantum devices
assertions.certainty_reason: One study with two small QNN architectures; empirical.
assertions.reader_inference: Membership leakage is measurable in the tested QNNs; generality to other QML models is not shown.

assertions.value: The authors report that in HQNN simulations at Nshots = 16 the MIA success rate fell sharply while classification accuracy fell only slightly.
quotes: as the measurement count decreases to Nshots = 16, the MIA success rate displays extreme sensitivity to noise, decreasing from
the model's classification accuracy demonstrates remarkable robustness, decreasing only slightly from
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation result on one architecture; the exact percentages follow the quoted words in the source and are left out here.

assertions.value: The authors report that the SSD unlearning method performs poorly on the basic QNN but achieves significantly better outcomes on the HQNN.
quotes: The results demonstrate that the SSD method performs poorly on the basic QNN model but achieves significantly better outcomes on the HQNN model.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the work uses hardware-efficient ansatz with a 5layer depth and focuses on class-level unlearning, where all data of a particular class are unlearned.
quotes: both using hardware-efficient ansatz with a 5layer depth
In this work, we focus on class-level unlearning, where all data belonging to a particular class are to be unlearned.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup and scope (Sec. IV, QMU workflow).

papers.title_in_file: Embedding of Tree Tensor Networks into Shallow Quantum Circuits
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Background 2.1-2.2, numerical results (Sec. 4), Conclusion; method details of Sec. 3 not read
papers.what_it_is: Proposes a method to embed tree tensor networks into shallow two-qubit-gate circuits as a way to initialize variational circuits.

assertions.value: The authors report that for the Heisenberg model ground state, TTN embeddings outperform MPS embeddings in both shallow and deep circuits, while MPS excels in the intermediate region.
quotes: The result of the J1-J2 Heisenberg model reveals an intriguing pattern: TTN outperforms in both shallow and deep quantum circuits, while MPS excels in the intermediate region.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical numerical result on two small datasets.

assertions.value: The authors state that applying their method to various TTNs prepares quantum circuit parameters with better accuracy than embedding MPSs.
quotes: confirmed that it prepares quantum circuit parameters with better accuracy than embedding MPSs.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author summary of numerical results; no hardware run.
assertions.reader_inference: The result is for state-vector embedding accuracy, not for avoiding barren plateaus in a trained VQA.

assertions.value: The authors state that the comparison uses tensor networks of bond dimension eight with 1000 optimization steps, and a Heisenberg model with J2/J1 = 0.5.
quotes: The bond dimensions of tensor networks are eight and the number of optimization steps is 1000.
In this paper, we utilized J2/J1 = 0.5.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup (Sec. 4).

papers.title_in_file: Differentiable Quantum Architecture Search for Quantum Reinforcement Learning
papers.partial_detail: Whole paper read except related-work equations
papers.what_it_is: Applies differentiable quantum architecture search (DQAS) to quantum deep Q-learning on CartPole and FrozenLake.

assertions.value: The authors report that the automatically designed architecture improves performance by about 200% over the manual baseline, lowering the average solving point from around 800 to 400 for cart pole and 1000 to 400 for frozen lake.
quotes: The automatically-designed architecture (green lines) improves the performance by about 200% compared to the baseline, decreasing the average solving point from around 800 to 400 for the cart pole and 1000 to 400 for the frozen lake.
assertions.certainty_reason: Small simulation study on two toy environments.
assertions.reader_inference: The 200% figure is the authors' wording for a halving of the solving point.

assertions.value: The authors state that the performance of the designed circuit depends on whether the corresponding super-circuit learns well during training.
quotes: Consequently, the performance of the designed circuit depends on whether the corresponding super-circuit learns well during the training process.
assertions.certainty_reason: Observed in two super-circuits only.

assertions.value: The authors state the work uses four qubits and a shallow super-circuit of one parameterized block repeated five times with a minimal learning-step training, and that a better architecture might hide in a deep super-circuit.
assertions.anchor: Sec. IV A and Sec. V
quotes: This work uses four qubits and repeats one parameterized block five times to create the super-circuit.
This work uses a shallow super-circuit and mini-learningstep for the training process.
However, better architecture might hide in a deep super-circuit.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup and limit (Sec. IV A, Sec. V).

papers.title_in_file: Utilizing Graph Sparsification for Pre-processing in Maxcut QUBO Solver
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Sec. 2-3 theorems, Sec. 4.4 discussion, Conclusion; experiment tables skimmed
papers.what_it_is: Proposes edge sampling by effective resistance before sending maxcut QUBO problems to cloud classical or quantum-inspired solvers.

assertions.value: The paper proves that, assuming an exact QUBO solver, solving the sparsified graph gives an approximation algorithm for the max cut problem, with a factor set by the sparsification parameter epsilon.
quotes: -approximation algorithm for the max cut problem.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 3.1, Sec. 3, follows from Theorem 2.1 cited from [46].

assertions.value: The authors report that on classical and quantum-inspired solvers the method consistently yields an approximation ratio of about 0.9 with communication cost reductions between 60% and 95%.
quotes: consistently yields solutions with an approximation ratio of about 0.9, while simultaneously achieving a significant reduction in communication costs to cloud servers, ranging between 60% and 95%.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on public benchmark graphs.

assertions.value: The authors state that they confined experiments to smaller instances and that expanding experiments to include quantum solvers is future work.
quotes: Therefore, we confined our experimentation to smaller instances
In our future research, we plan to expand our experiments to include quantum solvers.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope and limit (Sec. 4.4, Sec. 5).

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Fisher kernel for mitigating the vanishing similarity issue
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, main-text results, numerical experiments, Conclusion; Supplementary proofs not read
papers.what_it_is: Proposes quantum Fisher kernels and shows analytically and numerically that one variant avoids vanishing similarity with alternating layered ansatz.

assertions.value: The paper derives that with the alternating layered ansatz the variance of the ALDQFK quantity does not depend on the total number of qubits but on the unitary block size and the depth of the local block.
quotes: Moreover, in the case (2) where the ALA is used, the variance does not depend on the total number of qubits, but the size of the unitary block m and the depth d of the local unitary block
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 1 under a design assumption on the circuits (main text).

assertions.value: The authors state that the numerical experiments confirm the vanishing similarity issue for the fidelity-based QK in Proposition 1 and the validity of Theorem 1.
quotes: Overall, the numerical experiments confirm the vanishing similarity issue in the Fidelity-based QK in Proposition 1, and the validity of Theorem 1 in the main result.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation result; the paper itself notes deviations.

assertions.value: The authors report that the ALDQFK variance with HEA looks inconsistent with Theorem 1 (1), which they attribute to the 2-design assumption not being satisfied.
quotes: We remark that the variance of the ALDQFK with HEA does not decrease exponentially fast, which looks inconsistent to Theorem 1 (1).
This is because the assumption on the 2-design property of quantum circuits is not satisfied due to the insufficient expressivity of the quantum circuits
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation observation and the authors' explanation.

papers.title_in_file: Light-cone feature selection for quantum machine learning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Sec. 3.1, 3.3, Conclusion and Discussion; Sec. 2 formalism skimmed
papers.what_it_is: Proposes selecting light-cones of quantum kernel models as features, shown on four toy tasks.

assertions.value: The authors state they numerically demonstrate the method on four applications using toy tasks.
quotes: We numerically demonstrate its versatility for four different applications using toy tasks
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope in the abstract.

assertions.value: The authors report that pruning to the largest-weight light-cone leaves the KTA value nearly unchanged: PQK 0.605 to 0.600, QFK 0.987 to 0.983.
quotes: the performances of the pruned models are comparable to the original models; the KTA value of PQKs (QFKs) just decreases from 0.605 to 0.600 (0.987 to 0.983) by pruning.
assertions.certainty_reason: One toy task, simulation.

assertions.value: The authors state the classical cost of kernel estimation scales at least quadratically with the number of training points, and that the technique might not work in the classically-hard regime.
quotes: the classical computational cost for the quantum kernel estimation scales at least quadratically with respect to the number of training data points
our technique might not work in the classically-hard regime
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limits (Sec. 4).

papers.title_in_file: Quantum support vector machines for classification and regression on a trapped-ion quantum computer
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Sec. 2.3 QSVC on IonQ Harmony, Sec. 3 Discussion, start of Sec. 4; regression and appendices skimmed
papers.what_it_is: QSVC and QSVR experiments on simulators and the IonQ Harmony trapped-ion processor, including a credit card fraud dataset.

assertions.value: The authors report test accuracies on the IonQ Harmony of 70% for the credit-card dataset and 100% for the MNIST and Fashion-MNIST datasets, equivalent to noiseless quantum kernels.
quotes: Test accuracies achieved with the quantum computer for the credit-card dataset, the MNIST dataset, and the Fashion-MNIST dataset were 70%, 100%, and 100%, respectively, reflecting equivalent performance to the QSVC models using noiseless quantum kernels.
assertions.certainty_reason: Hardware run on very small samples.
assertions.reader_inference: The training and test sets are tiny, so the accuracies carry little statistical weight.

assertions.value: The authors state the QSVC model used 20 data points for training and 10 for testing, with 500 measurements per kernel entry.
quotes: we used 20 data points for training and 10 data points (which are separate from the training data) for testing.
the number of quantum measurements per kernel entry was set to 500
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup (Sec. 4.1).

assertions.value: The authors state their quantum feature map did not necessarily exemplify a quantum advantage because of its shallow circuit and limited number of qubits.
quotes: While our quantum feature map did not necessarily exemplify a so-called quantum advantage because of its shallow quantum circuit and the limited number of qubits
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limit (Sec. 3).

papers.title_in_file: A Practitioner's Guide to Quantum Algorithms for Optimisation Problems
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Conclusion; body sections on annealing, QAOA and QAOA variants skimmed by search only
papers.what_it_is: Review of quantum optimisation methods (annealing, QAOA, QAOA variants) for newcomers.

assertions.value: The authors state that in practice there has been no realisation of the potential advantage in quantum optimisation and that there are many reasons to be sceptical that it is close.
quotes: However, in practice there has been no realisation of this potential advantage and there are many reasons to be sceptical that such advantage is even close to being achieved.
assertions.certainty_reason: Review author assessment, no single study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the small number of qubits limits studied problems to regimes that, for all optimisation problems of real world interest, are efficiently solvable classically.
quotes: the small number of qubits available limits the size of problems that can be studied to regimes that, for all optimisation problems of real world interest, are efficiently solvable classically.
assertions.certainty_reason: Review author assessment, no single study.

assertions.value: The authors state the paper aims to give a comprehensive overview of the theory of quantum optimisation techniques and their practical application, focusing on near-term potential for NISQ devices.
quotes: This paper aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the theory of quantum optimisation techniques and their practical application, focusing on their near-term potential for noisy intermediate scale quantum devices.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope in the abstract.
